content:
The setting that controls what happens with deleted messages is found at <Account Settings | Server Settings | Server Settings | When I delete a message...>. This is a per-account setting.

The Spam folder is a special server folder and can't be deleted, but you can remove it from the list of folders in Thunderbird. To do this, right click on the account name in the Folders list, and from the pop-up context menu choose "Subscribe...". Uncheck the box next to the Spam/Junk folder, then choose OK. Keep in mind that if the server moves anything to the Spam folder you won't see it unless you go to web mail.

If you're not using the Spam folder feature, it's probably best to turn off the setting <Settings | Privacy & Security | Spam | When messages are marked as spam:>

content:
Are you seeing any error messages?

Do you see the missing messages on the Gmail web mail page?

Are you absolutely sure it hasn't downloaded anything? Is it possible messages wound up in an unexpected folder due to a message filter or a misconfiguration? See <Account Settings | Synchronization & Storage> for some settings that could affect this.

It's also possible that Quick Filter can be set to hide messages.

Have you used Thunderbird's search features to search for a known, missing message?

If you've double-checked all that stuff and are confident that it's not a settings issue, I'd be inclined to delete the account and re-create it. Keep in mind that this will download all messages on the server. When you do this, also delete any saved passwords for that account. You will be asked to re-authorize when you next start Thunderbird.

It would be good to make a backup copy of your Thunderbird profile before deleting the account. Since it's an IMAP account there should be no danger of data loss, but you never know. And regular backups are a good practice.

content: If you mean the password for you email account (Gmail, Yahoo, etc.) you might be able to see it in <Settings | Privacy & Security | Passwords | Saved Passwords>. However, depending on your server authentication settings, you may only see a randomized token, which appears as a random string of characters, but not your actual password. If so, and you have no other record of your password, you will have to reset it on your email provider's web site. You should then be prompted for the new password when you next start Thunderbird.

https://www.xfinity.com/support/articles/email-client-programs-with-xfinity-email

You have port 587, but they specify port 465, and, in fact that's what I successfully use. So, change the port and see if you get better results.
